data.description:
kno 0.17.2. When a lease is TERMINATED while still BOUND to a knot sitting in an action state, that knot has no legal transition left through the normal verbs:

  - kno claim <id>    -> 'is in state <action>, which is not a claimable queue state'
  - kno next <id>     -> 'bound lease is in state lease_terminated -- expected lease_active'
  - kno next <id> (no --lease) -> 'knot has a bound lease; rerun with --lease <lease-id>'
  - kno rollback <id> -> same lease_terminated rejection (rollback is the documented recovery
                         path, so the one verb meant to unstick a knot is itself blocked by
                         the condition it should recover from)
  - kno lease extend  -> 'cannot extend a terminated or expired lease'
  - a fresh lease     -> 'lease mismatch: knot has <old>, caller provided <new>'

Observed 2026-07-26 on knot quilt-9f51 in the quilt repo, bound lease 41da. The lease's own
record shows created_at 07:09:40.005088Z and updated_at (termination) 07:09:40.117997Z — it
was terminated ~113ms after creation, during the very claim that bound it, while that claim
also emitted a knots-worktree sync error:

  git -C /Users/cartine/quilt/.knots/_worktree checkout knots
  fatal: 'knots' is already used by worktree at '/Users/cartine/quilt/.knots/_worktree'

The claim still advanced the knot into 'planning', so the knot moved while its lease died —
the two are not committed together. A later 'kno update -H' on that knot SUCCEEDED against
the dead lease; only 'next' and 'rollback' enforce lease liveness. That inconsistency is
part of the bug: an agent gets no signal that its lease is gone until it tries to advance,
by which time the knot is already wedged.

There IS an escape hatch — 'kno state <id> <state> [--force]' — but nothing in the error
messages of claim/next/rollback mentions it, so an agent following the documented
claim/next/rollback loop concludes the knot is unrecoverable and escalates to a human.

This is the third lease death observed in one session; the other two were recoverable only
because those knots happened to be sitting in claimable queue states at the time.
